sec: Vitamin D metabolism and drugs affecting it · p869

items.q: The plant source of vitamin D is:
items.exp: Plant source = ergocalciferol; animal/skin/diet = cholecalciferol (vit D3). (Book p869)

items.q: The liver enzyme converting cholecalciferol to calcidiol is:
items.exp: Liver vit D3 25-hydroxylase makes calcidiol/25-OH D3. (Book p869)

items.q: The form used to MEASURE blood vitamin D levels (long t½, major circulating/storage form) is:
items.exp: Calcidiol has long t½, is the major circulating & storage form, and is used to measure vit D levels. (Book p869)

items.q: The inactive shunt product formed by 24-α-hydroxylase is:
The renal (PCT) enzyme making the ACTIVE form, stimulated by PTH, is:
items.exp: Kidney PCT 1α-hydroxylase (activated by PTH) makes 1,25-dihydroxycholecalciferol/calcitriol (active). (Book p869)

items.q: Calcitriol in intestinal epithelium induces which trio to absorb calcium?
opts: Calcium-binding protein, calcium-stimulated ATPase, alkaline phosphatase
TRPV5/6 channels alone at the membrane
items.exp: It induces calcium-binding protein, calcium-stimulated ATPase and alkaline phosphatase → intestinal Ca absorption → raises plasma Ca, inhibiting PTH. (Book p869)

items.q: Match drug to vitamin D effect — 1) Phenytoin  2) INH  3) Steroids & ketoconazole … A) Inhibits 25-hydroxylase  B) Causes vit D resistance  C) Inhibit 1α-hydroxylase
items.exp: Phenytoin causes vit D resistance; INH inhibits 25-hydroxylase; steroids & ketoconazole inhibit 1α-hydroxylase. (Book p869)

items.q: ‘In nephrotic syndrome, vitamin D binding globulin is lost in urine while the vitamin D level stays normal.’
items.exp: Vit D binding globulin is lost in urine in nephrotic syndrome (vit D level normal). (Book p869)
